clue.text: Leave the last of citrus jam

indicators.note: asks for the final letter of the word that follows it

parts.note: to jam things into a space is to cram them in

explanation.surface: Someone is told to leave the final spoonful of marmalade for others.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal synonym: to go away quickly, usually said as an order.

clue.text: Make-up — very little — applied carelessly

parts.note: slap is British slang for cosmetics, especially theatrical ones
a dash is a tiny amount, as of milk or sauce

explanation.surface: A touch of cosmetics has been put on in a hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: An adjective for work done hastily and without attention, as paint thrown on.

clue.text: Case of rickets interrupting show is a setback

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into something, so the two letters go inside the word for show

parts.note: to show something is to reveal it

indicators.note: a case is an outer covering, so take the first and last letters of the next word

explanation.surface: A performance has to stop when someone is found to have a bone disease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case of rickets' reads as a patient with the bone disease, but 'Case of' asks only for the outside of the word, and 'interrupting' places that within the word for show.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a change of fortune for the worse.

clue.text: Serviceman spied jumping up and down

indicators.note: letters that jump leap out of their places, so the two words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A soldier was seen bouncing on the spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumping up and down' reads as one action, but 'jumping' alone rearranges SERVICEMAN SPIED, leaving 'up and down' as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An older clinical term for bipolar, describing moods that swing between elation and despair.

clue.text: Instrument company flying through sum of money

parts.note: BA is British Airways, the UK's flag-carrier airline
by can mean through, as in 'by hard work'
a grand is slang for a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: A maker of musical instruments is burning through its cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instrument company' reads as one unit, but the split falls after 'Instrument': the company is one that flies, British Airways.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a small horizontal piano is a musical instrument.

clue.text: Dairy product's not long-lasting, for the most part

indicators.note: most of a word is all but its final letter, so the last one is dropped

parts.note: something brief does not last long

explanation.surface: Milk and cheese generally go off quite quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the most part' drops F from the end of BRIEF.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a soft French cheese is made from milk.

clue.text: Will's character: something he has to say is what matters

parts.note: Will is William Shakespeare, and Bottom is the weaver in his A Midsummer Night's Dream
a character in a play has a line to speak

explanation.surface: William is a man of principle whose opinions carry real weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' is Shakespeare on first-name terms, and 'character' is one of his roles, not a person's nature.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom from accounts: the final figure, hence the essential point.

clue.text: Tail of whiting hugely in fashion for foodies?

indicators.note: the tail is the back end, so take the final letter of the next word

parts.note: prices that rise astronomically rise hugely

explanation.surface: The rear end of a small fish has become enormously trendy among gourmets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in fashion' is not trendiness here but 'in the manner': the definition is an adverb, with the question mark admitting the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: An adverb meaning in the way of people devoted to fine eating.

clue.text: Plan military commander keeps close

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it, so the commander's title holds the other word inside

parts.note: an aga was a military commander in the Ottoman Empire
the close of something is its end

explanation.surface: A general holds his strategy near to his chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeps close' reads as one phrase, but 'close' is a noun meaning conclusion, and 'keeps' has AGA hold it.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a list of things to be done or discussed.

clue.text: Recorded absorbing intro from radio, turning set off

indicators.note: to turn is to face the other way, and in a down clue the whole assembly is read from the bottom up
to absorb is to take in, so the recorded word takes the letter inside

parts.note: something recorded on a cassette was taped

indicators.note: an intro is an opening, so take the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone tapes the opening of a broadcast, then swivels round and switches the receiver off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absorbing' puts R inside TAPED to make TRAPED, and 'turning' reads that backwards. 'set off' is to begin a journey, not to switch a radio set off.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to leave on a journey.

clue.text: A very boring medic and Christian

indicators.note: to bore is to drill into something, so the letter for very goes inside the medic

parts.note: a dentist is a medical practitioner for teeth

explanation.surface: A doctor who is both extremely dull and devout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' looks like a description of the medic but is the insertion signal: V drills into DENTIST. The drilling suits the dentist nicely.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a member of a Protestant denomination expecting the Second Coming is one kind of believer in Christ.

clue.text: Adventure tale with record group of followers

parts.note: She is H. Rider Haggard's 1887 adventure novel
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: An exciting story that broke sales figures has won a band of devoted fans.
explanation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: people who follow others without thinking are likened to a flock.

clue.text: Perhaps make TV programme presenting no diversion?

definitions.meaning: to be in charge of filming a show, one way of making it
describes a route that goes straight there with no detour

explanation.surface: A broadcaster might produce a show that offers no entertainment at all.
explanation.definitionFit: One word is both the verb for overseeing a production and the adjective for a straight, uninterrupted route.

clue.text: My gold boxes free in passage

indicators.note: to box something is to enclose it, so the first two pieces together surround the third

parts.note: My! and Cor! are both exclamations of surprise, cor being British slang
OR is gold in heraldry
to rid someone of something is to free them of it

explanation.surface: Someone's crates of bullion are travelling at no charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' is not a possessive here but an exclamation of surprise, and 'boxes' is a verb, not crates: the exclamation and the gold together enclose the word for free.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a long narrow hallway is a way through a building.

clue.text: The digit between numbers three and five?

definitions.text: The digit between numbers three and five?

parts.words: The digit between numbers three and five?
parts.note: digit suggests the numeral four, but it is the body part that comes fourth on the hand when the thumb is counted first

explanation.definitionFit: The fourth digit of the hand, where a wedding band is worn, sits between the middle one and the little one.

clue.text: Wrong turns in two countries where Americans dwell

indicators.note: places the turned word within the pair of countries, between them

parts.note: a state is a country
a land is a country

indicators.note: to turn is to face the other way, so the word for wrong is read backwards

parts.note: a sin is a moral wrong

explanation.surface: A traveller keeps taking bad turnings in a pair of nations full of Americans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrong turns' reads as bad turnings, but 'Wrong' is a noun and 'turns' is the verb sending it backwards; 'in' then sets it between the two countries.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: it is one of New York City's five boroughs, home to about half a million people.

clue.text: Political writer accepting his own name for putrid substance

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the writer's surname takes his first name inside

parts.note: Thomas Paine wrote Rights of Man and Common Sense
Paine's first name Thomas is familiarly Tom

explanation.surface: A pamphleteer agrees to be known by the label 'rotten stuff'.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of foul-smelling compounds formed when protein rots, once blamed for food poisoning.

clue.text: Sprayed your somewhat black clothes

indicators.note: as a verb, to clothe is to wrap round, so the scorched word wraps the short form of your

parts.note: something singed is lightly burnt and so slightly blackened
YR is a written abbreviation of your

explanation.surface: Somebody has squirted liquid over your charcoal-coloured outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'black clothes' reads as dark garments, but 'clothes' is a verb: the scorched word dresses the shortened 'your'.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: squirted with liquid from a tube and plunger, as ears or plants are.

clue.text: Got in more rubbish in essay subject

indicators.note: places the jumbled letters inside the word for essay

parts.note: to essay something is to try it

indicators.note: rubbish is a mess, so the three words before it are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A pupil has stuffed even more nonsense into a piece of written coursework.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rubbish' makes IGONOMETR from GOT IN MORE, and the second 'in' puts that inside TRY. 'essay' is the verb meaning attempt, not a piece of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the mathematics of triangles and angles is a school discipline.

clue.text: Person using computers etc. After tot

indicators.note: says the computing piece comes later than the word for tot

parts.note: to tot up figures is to add them
ICT is information and communications technology, the British school name for computing

explanation.surface: Somebody goes on the laptop once they have had a small drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Person using computers' looks like the definition, but it stops at 'using', which alone means taking drugs; 'After' orders the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A drug user in the dependent sense: someone hooked on a substance.

clue.text: Exercise with body part raised

parts.note: an arm is a limb of the body
something raised is up

explanation.surface: A gym move performed holding a limb in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: gentle stretching done before the main activity.

clue.text: Screen rebel's in post in college

parts.note: James Dean starred in the film Rebel Without a Cause; the possessive gives his name plus S
in and hip both mean fashionable

explanation.surface: A film outlaw has taken up a job at a university.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'in' is not a container signal: it means fashionable, giving HIP.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the office held by a senior fellow in charge of discipline or a faculty.

clue.text: Criminal strategy to get apparently good food

parts.note: a scam is a dishonest scheme to cheat people
pi is old slang for pious, making a show of being virtuous

explanation.surface: A crook has a plan for obtaining a meal that looks tasty.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: breaded langoustine tails are a dish served in pubs and restaurants.

clue.text: Not yet settled on time for pair-work?

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece on another sits above it, so the first piece comes before the letter for time

parts.note: a bill that is due is owed and still unpaid
T is the physics abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Nobody has fixed a slot yet for the exercise done in twos.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of music written for two performers.

clue.text: This person likes male and female feet

parts.note: the setter speaking of themselves says I
someone attracted to both sexes would say 'am bi', short for bisexual

explanation.surface: The speaker has a fondness for the feet of men and women alike.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole phrase is a statement in the first person, 'I am bi', run together. The feet are metrical ones in verse, not body parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Examples in the plural: each is a unit of verse with a short syllable then a long one.

clue.text: Boiled food, fish that's tough

parts.note: gruel is thin porridge made by boiling oats in water or milk
a ling is a long-bodied fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A plate of poached seafood turns out to be chewy.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym in the sense of arduous: an exhausting task is a hard one.

clue.text: Very sensitive with respect to going wrong

indicators.note: something that goes wrong ends up out of order, so the letters before it are disordered

explanation.surface: Someone is extremely touchy about anything to do with making mistakes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with respect to' reads as one phrase, but 'with' only joins: 'going wrong' rearranges RESPECT TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A security classification: information so delicate that it has the highest restriction.

clue.text: Return from east, idly wandering around

indicators.note: the jumbled word goes round the letter for east
to wander is to stray from position, so the letters of the word before it move about

parts.note: E is the compass abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: A traveller comes back from the Orient after roaming aimlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' turns IDLY into YILD, and 'around' wraps it round E. 'Return' is the financial noun, not a journey home.
explanation.definitionFit: A financial synonym: what an investment pays back to its holder.
